verdict.rationale: Jitsu Functions are documented as JavaScript/TypeScript code that runs in the pipeline before delivery to destinations, explicitly covering filter, transform and enrich. Enrichment is backed by the Fetch API, Warehouse API and persistent storage, and development is supported by a debugger on sample data plus a CLI that scaffolds a tested project and deploys it. An old HN comment saying Functions didn't seem present is an impression from launch time, not a concrete hands-on failure, so it does not dispute the docs. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of Functions working in production.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can transform, filter, and enrich events in-pipeline with custom code or functions before they reach destinations

citations.quote: Functions are designed to process data in Jitsu before it is sent to the destination. These functions, written in JavaScript, provide various data handling options
Filter - Exclude data that fails to meet your specified criteria. Transform - Modify data to fit the schema of your destination. Enrich - Add extra information to the event.
Filter, transform, and enrich events with TypeScript functions before they land.
Fetch API - Perform HTTP requests to third-party services. Warehouse API - Query your data warehouses.
Jitsu comes with a functions debugger/editor that allows to run function on a sample data
